historical_basis.quote: A banshee (/ˈbænʃiː/ BAN-shee; Modern Irish bean sí  [bʲanˠ ˈʃiː] , from Old Irish: ben síde  [bʲen ˈʃiːðʲe] , "woman of the fairy mound" or "fairy woman") is a female spirit in Irish folklore who heralds the death of a family member

statement.id: Banshee adalah roh perempuan dalam cerita rakyat Irlandia yang menandai kematian anggota keluarga.
statement.en: A banshee is a female spirit in Irish folklore who heralds the death of a family member.

historical_basis.quote: Sometimes she has long streaming hair, which she may be seen combing, with some legends specifying she can only keen while combing her hair.

statement.id: Banshee kadang terlihat memiliki rambut panjang terurai yang sedang disisir.

historical_basis.quote: She wears a grey cloak over a green dress, and her eyes are red from continual weeping.

NO human face, hands, torso, costume, horns or hybrid anatomy. Background old Irish stone cottage window with faint distant warm candle glow, evening mist over dark river and deep forest green countryside, walnut weathered masonry, subtle antique gold rim lighting. Refined naturalistic premium oil-painted texture and detailed iridescent black feathers. Bird alone; no other animals, people, bodies or victims. No magical jewels, crown, weapons, gore, text, inscription, signature, frame or watermark. This is one source-attested animal manifestation of the banshee, whose role is to mourn and foretell death, not cause it. Preserve that sorrowful herald aura.
